equity_bridge.item: Minority interests at 18x FY2025 minority profit (EUR 127m; book 745.4m)
equity_bridge.note: NCI charged once, in the bridge; flows are 100% consolidated. Annual FY2025 line 3526, H1 2026 line 1297.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: medium-term organic growth between the 5yr equity CAGR (7.2%, inflated by 2022 energy pass-through and the Airgas-era balance sheet) and the flat owner-FCF series; BEYOND's ~5% includes bolt-on M&A that is not in these flows
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3yr revenue CAGR is -3.5% while 3yr EPS is +8.3% and equity +3.4%: FY2022 revenue (EUR 29.9bn) was inflated by energy cost pass-through at near-zero margin, so the 3yr revenue figure understates underlying growth (comparable growth was +2-4%/yr). 5yr figures (revenue 5.6%, EPS 7.4%, equity 7.2%) are within 30% of each other; no structural divergence.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs are restated for the one-for-ten free share attributions of 2022 and 2024 (FY2020 EPS 5.14 -> 4.25; FY2022 5.27 -> 4.79) against reported FY2025 EPS of 6.08 (pre the June 2026 attribution). Owner FCF = OCF - capex - lease payments - SBC: FY2020 ~2,272, FY2022 ~2,217, FY2025 2,324. Owner-FCF CAGR (0.5%/1.6%) is slightly below reported FCF CAGR (0.8%/1.8%) because SBC rose from 38.5 to 69.2 - immaterial. The real story is capex: 2,630 (FY2020) -> 3,843 (FY2025), +7.9%/yr, absorbing all of the EBITDA growth (5,928 -> 8,145, +6.6%/yr). FCF is flat because the company is in an investment cycle (record EUR 6.0bn backlog), not because the business has stopped growing.

scenario_narratives.base: Air Liquide keeps doing what it has done since 2022: roughly +60bps of EBITDA margin a year from pricing, portfolio pruning and efficiency, reaching ~33% by FY2030 (about +300bps of operating margin against the +400-600bps BEYOND ambition), with ~4% organic revenue growth from Electronics/AI fabs, US reshoring and Healthcare on top of the DIG Airgas scope. Capex intensity eases from 14% to 12% as the EUR 6bn backlog converts into take-or-pay revenue. The margin gap to Linde narrows but does not close. Discounted at a 7% EUR WACC with a 20x terminal cap, this is worth materially less than the ~29x earnings the market pays; the price implies a discount rate nearer 5.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The BEYOND plan is delivered in full under activist scrutiny: +550bps operating margin by 2030, growth at the top of the range on the AI semiconductor cycle and reshoring, and capital intensity falls as ROCE passes 11%. Even so, the model grants only a 20x terminal multiple at 7%, so the bull value sits below the current price - the market is already pricing the bull case plus a lower discount rate.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Linde gap is structural. Margin improvement stalls at +150bps, European industrial demand and helium remain headwinds, hydrogen projects are rescoped, capex intensity stays high and the balance sheet (45% D/E plus a EUR 4bn buyback) absorbs the shortfall. Growth 2-2.5% published.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Air Liquide is a high-quality, long-duration cash compounder - 15-20 year take-or-pay contracts, an oligopoly, cost pass-through - but FCF has been flat for five years because capex absorbs all of the EBITDA growth, and the market prices it as a bond proxy at ~29x earnings and ~15x EV/EBITDA. The house model values the owner FCF the business actually produces, charges SBC, leases and minorities once each, discounts at a EUR-built 7% and caps the terminal multiple at 20x. On that basis even the bull case is below the current price: the market is paying for both full delivery of the BEYOND margin plan and a discount rate well below 7%. The required-return table is the key output - it shows what IRR today's price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: the 20x cap binds in all scenarios; the market's ~15x EV/EBITDA on this asset implies closer to 30x FCF. Removing the cap at 7%/2.5% lifts value ~10%; granting the market's multiple roughly doubles it.
Discount rate: a 1pt change in WACC moves the base value by ~20%; a 5.5-6% rate reconciles the model to the price.
Margin delivery vs. Linde: each 100bps of EBITDA margin is worth ~EUR 7-8/share at maturity; the bear-bull spread is almost entirely margin.
Capex intensity: the model assumes intensity falls from 14% to 12%; if the energy-transition backlog keeps it at 14%, base-case FCF is ~15% lower.

Energy pass-through and FX distort published revenue and margins year to year; the drivers are set on an ex-energy basis and a given year can miss by 2-3pts on either metric without the thesis changing.
Net debt anchor is the post-dividend, post-DIG June 2026 figure; the December 2026 balance sheet will likely show EUR 1-1.5bn less net debt (worth ~EUR 2/share).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 140.78-182.26
data_sources.financials: AI.PA_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, EUR millions, FY2014-FY2025 + H1 FY2011-H1 FY2026); FY2025 Universal Registration Document and H1 2026 half-year financial report for net debt, share count, NCI, leases, SBC and guidance
data_sources.qualitative: AI.PA_Analysis.json (2026-10-25), incl. the 5 Oct 2026 Capital Markets Day BEYOND plan and Elliott Management's stake

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average used for H1 2026 diluted EPS (637,823,581; H1 2026 report note 9.2), after the one-for-ten free share attribution of 10 June 2026 (59.5m new shares). Shares in issue ex-treasury at 30 June 2026 were 636,603,516. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; the announced EUR 4bn buyback is value-neutral in this model (cash out = shares in at market) and is not modelled as a count reduction.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Universal Registration Document, consolidated statement of changes in equity 'Share-based payments' EUR 69.2m (AI.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:13426); the personnel-expense note shows EUR 43.2m (line 14587) - the equity-statement figure is used because it also captures the biennial discounted employee share offering. No net-share-settlement tax line exists (French free-share plans); no separate equity-award tax to add.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchase of treasury shares EUR 4.0m (line 13363); H1 2026 EUR 163.1m. The EUR 4bn BEYOND buyback is an authorisation, not spend - recorded here as zero until cash leaves the financing line.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:11Z regular close (Euronext Paris); valuation on Sunday 2026-10-25 so this is the latest close
inputs.net_debt_note: Net debt EUR 13,921m at 30 June 2026 per the H1 2026 report (gross borrowings 15,982.1 less cash 2,061.2 = 13,920.9, ties to the reported figure). Air Liquide's net-debt definition EXCLUDES IFRS 16 lease liabilities (EUR 1,276.8m) - consistent with lease treatment (B) below. The June figure is post the ~EUR 3bn DIG Airgas acquisition (Jan 2026) and post the EUR 2.2bn May dividend; FY2025 net debt was 8,416m. Using the latest balance sheet is conservative by roughly the H2 seasonal cash build.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate. Risk-free ~3.3% (10y OAT; Bund ~2.7%), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.85 -> cost of equity ~7.5%; pre-tax cost of debt 3.0% (reported average cost of net debt H1 2026), after-tax ~2.3%; D/(D+E) at market ~11% (EUR 111bn market cap vs 13.9bn net debt) -> CAPM WACC ~6.9%, rounded to 7.0%. Same 7.0% in all three scenarios: cyclicality, execution and leverage risk are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost (principal 232.7 + interest 48.9 = EUR 281.6m FY2025, 1.05% of revenue; the cash-flow statement's 'Lease liabilities repayments and net interests paid on lease liabilities' line of 283m) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.0%; lease liabilities (1,276.8m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation: total D&A 2,563.5 less ROU depreciation proxied by lease principal repayments 232.7 = 2,330.8 (8.65% of revenue); da_pct_path 9.0% allows for DIG Airgas's own D&A and the PPA amortisation that started in 2026.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (the engine builds from Group EBITDA). Minority interests are charged ONCE, in the equity bridge, at 18x the FY2025 minority share of net profit (EUR 127m, Annual FY2025 line 3526; H1 2026 64m) = EUR -2,290m, c. 3x the 745.4m book value - 18x is in line with the base-case implied P/E, so the NCI is valued on the same basis as the Group. Equity-accounted associates are immaterial (share of profit well under 1% of EBITDA) and are left in place.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: The Metrics CSV free_cash_flow (OCF 6,518.4 - capex 3,843.4 = 2,675.0) is BEFORE lease payments and AFTER interest, because Air Liquide classifies the cost of net debt inside operating cash flow (IAS 7.35 footnote, H1 2026 report). reported_fcf here is Air Liquide's own definition before disposals: 2,675.0 - 281.6 lease payments = 2,393.4; last_fcf = 2,393.4 - 69.2 SBC = 2,324.2 (owner FCF, levered, 8.6% of revenue). The engine's projection is UNLEVERED (EBITDA -> SBC -> lease -> D&A -> tax -> capex -> WC) and deducts net debt in the bridge; adding back ~EUR 180m after-tax interest to last_fcf gives ~2,500m, which ties to the component build's FY0 owner FCF within working-capital noise.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping under the BEYOND plan through FY2030, so a 5-year capitalisation would freeze an immature margin). Routing: operating company, non-US, industrial with IFRS 16 leases and a minority interest -> owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md (a1 currency-matched WACC, b lease treatment, c NCI, f risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker. FY0 = FY2025 (last completed year); Y1 = FY2026, discounted a full period per the folder's end-of-year convention. Y1 growth includes the DIG Airgas scope (~EUR 900m revenue; completed Jan 2026) so the EV from the flows is consistent with the June 2026 net debt that funded it. SBC is small (0.26% of revenue) but non-zero, so the house/street band is narrow rather than collapsed. Management's BEYOND targets (+400-600bps operating margin by 2030, ~5% revenue growth, ~10% EPS CAGR) are NOT taken at face value: the base case credits roughly +300bps and ~4% organic growth; the bull case credits ~+550bps; the bear case stalls at ~+150bps. Terminal cap 20x binds in every scenario (Gordon at 7%/2.5% = 22.8x) - the model deliberately does not grant the ~29x P/E / ~15x EV/EBITDA the market currently pays.

bear.narrative: The margin gap to Linde proves structural (business mix, European energy and labour, governance), not fixable: margin improvement stalls at ~+150bps by 2030. European Large Industries and Industrial Merchant stay soft, helium supply disruption persists, the clean-hydrogen backlog is rescoped or written down and capex intensity stays at ~13.5% to keep the installed base competitive. Published growth 2-2.5% with recurring FX drag. Leverage (45% D/E after DIG Airgas) plus the EUR 4bn buyback leaves less room for error. Terminal growth 2.0%; same 7% WACC.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +1.9% published: H1 was +0.8% published (+4.3% ex-currency/energy incl. DIG Airgas, +2.6% comparable) with a -3.6% FX drag; guidance is H2 growth similar to or slightly above H1 and the FX drag should ease against a weaker H2 2025 dollar base. FY2027-29 +4.0%: ~3% comparable Gas & Services growth (Electronics/AI fabs, US reshoring, Healthcare) plus start-ups from the EUR 6bn backlog, below BEYOND's ~5% which also counts bolt-on M&A not in these flows. Decays to 2.5% by Y9.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 30.2% (operating margin 20.7%). FY2026 +60bps to 30.8% (guided +100bps operating ex-energy and ex-PPA; some dilution from DIG mix and energy). Then +60bps/yr to 33.2% in FY2030 and 33.5% mature - roughly +300bps of operating margin vs the +400-600bps BEYOND ambition. Air Liquide has delivered +100bps/yr since 2022, so +60bps/yr of EBITDA margin for five more years is a continuation, not a leap; the full Linde-convergence case is the bull.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 capex 14.3% of revenue (3,843m); H1 2026 13.2%. BEYOND's >EUR 40bn 2026-30 allocation implies ~4bn/yr industrial capex. Intensity eases from 13.8% to 12.0% as the backlog converts to revenue and growth slows; terminal capex/D&A of 1.33x is consistent with 2.5% nominal growth in a capital-intensive asset base.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 ETR 24.6%, H1 2026 26.4% (French surcharge, non-deductible DIG costs). 25.5% in FY2026 then 25.0%; no NOLs or one-off credits in the base year.
base.wc_rationale: Industrial supplier: receivables and inventory exceed payables, so growth consumes cash. -5% of the revenue change; the company's active factoring programmes keep WCR small.

bull.narrative: BEYOND delivered as guided: +550bps operating margin by 2030 (EBITDA margin to ~36%, still below Linde's ~38-39%), revenue growth at the top of the 4-6% range as the AI/semiconductor Electronics cycle, US reshoring Large Industries contracts and DIG Airgas synergies all land, and capital intensity falls as the backlog converts and ROCE passes 11%. Elliott's pressure keeps the pricing and cost programme honest. Terminal growth 3.0%; same 7% WACC and 20x cap - the bull is in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20%: leverage has jumped to 45% D/E on the DIG Airgas acquisition while a EUR 4bn buyback and a record capex backlog are both committed, management itself cites reduced visibility, and the margin gap to Linde has persisted for a decade. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30%: the bull needs margin convergence, top-of-range growth AND falling capital intensity to land together, although Air Liquide's record of hitting its 2022-2025 margin targets, and Elliott's presence, keep it a genuine 30%. No live corporate action; the three-scenario frame holds.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
